# matplotlib

Python's plotting library. It appears in both lab repositories in two clearly different modes, and
the split is the interesting part.

## Mode 1 — interactive explorer (Discrete Maths)

In [[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] matplotlib is the *interface*, not the output format:

- **`GridSpec`** dashboards — several linked panels in one figure rather than separate plots, so a
  value and its cost are read together.
- **`Slider`** widgets over the parameters, in labs 2 and 4. Changing `m` and `n` and watching the
  recursive call count move is the deliverable — see [[ackermann-and-primitive-recursion]].
- **`LogNorm`** colour scaling on heatmaps, which is mandatory rather than cosmetic here: Ackermann
  values and factorization timings span so many orders of magnitude that a linear scale shows a
  single hot cell and nothing else.
- Benchmark curves for RSA attack runtime and success rate against key size —
  [[rsa-and-integer-factorization]].

This is [[make-the-formal-object-observable]] in library form.

## Mode 2 — headless figure generation (Python labs)

In [[python-programming-laboratories]] lab 11 it is a batch renderer inside a document pipeline:

- The **`Agg`** backend — no display, no GUI event loop, correct for a script that produces files.
- **`plt.close()` per figure**, across 41 chapters. Without it the figure manager retains every
  figure and memory climbs until the run dies; this is the standard matplotlib leak and the pipeline
  handles it explicitly.
- Output goes to a gitignored `charts/` directory, reproducible from source rather than committed.

Alongside [[pillow]] for cover images and BeautifulSoup for the source text, see
[[beautifulsoup]].

## Note

Neither repo pins a matplotlib version. In Discrete Maths it arrives with numpy as an ambient
scientific-Python assumption; in the Python labs it lives in the optional `labs` extra, keeping the
core package dependency-free — [[setuptools-and-pyproject]].
